title: Articulated connectors — native modeling preview
caption: Generic educational assembly, not a verified board or assembly instruction. Two instances reuse one connector definition; the latch rotates around a hinge, while the cable is a curved tube.

parts.label: Socket
parts.description: Generic rounded connector housing. Check actual manufacturer specifications before choosing hardware.

parts.label: Hinge
parts.description: The latch's parent frame rotates around the back-edge pivot, rather than translating the whole latch.

parts.label: Latch
parts.description: A beveled extruded polygon attached to the hinge frame. Its origin moves around the hinge pivot during the opening step.

objects.label: Curved cable
objects.description: A Catmull–Rom tube generated from bounded control points. It is explanatory, not a cable routing specification.

objects.label: Lathed part
objects.description: A surface of revolution from a radius/height profile.

steps.title: 1. Reusable assemblies
steps.narration: Two connectors reuse the same local part definition. This generic illustration is not verified hardware guidance. Click a part or choose it from the part list, then focus it or ask a question.

steps.title: 2. True hinge rotation
steps.narration: The left hinge rotates around its fixed local pivot. The attached latch follows that frame; its geometry moves around the hinge rather than rotating around its own center.

steps.title: 3. Both assemblies articulate
steps.narration: The second connector opens independently, retaining the first connector's pose. Curved cable and lathed geometry remain part of the same scene.
